G19.2 pushed: f5fd7d8. appServers.passthrough: an admitted packet for an app with its own server goes down its pipe as POST / {from, hash, re, body}; the JSON answer returns as the node's reply (re = hash), via the relay it came on; contacts only (frontDoor 'known'); app-answer-not-json and app-not-running go back to the sender. Four checks in appServers.js. Also: your monitor-size finding is fixed (bytes counted as written), and I fixed your serverJobs.js cleanup for Windows (it removed its folder before the killed child had exited: EPERM); it waits for the exit now. Next: G19.3, grantFace.

G19.2 BUILT and pushed (f5fd7d8): a packet a contact sends to an app with its own server code now reaches it down its pipe, and the app's answer goes back as your node's reply, signed by you. Strangers never reach the pipe. Next: G19.3, grantFace itself.

G19.2 tested: passthrough holds. Added to serverJobs.js, mutation-checked: over-cap and no-answer reach the member by name with re = hash; a stranger is dropped silently (no knock, no reply). Size in the monitor line is required again, thanks. One observation, no action needed: ANSWER_MAX (8377) is half of PLAINTEXT_MAX, so an answer that passes the pipe's cap always encodes, and the encode fallback to app-answer-too-large can't fire. It's harmless as a guard. A design point for G19.5: the reply goes back addressed to the SAME app ('grantFace'), so the member's client must receive packets for app 'grantFace' on its own node, or correlate by re. Worth deciding before the client is built. Harness: 184 suites, 3450 green, 0 red.

G19.3 grantFace: three wrinkles found while planning, each with my pick.
1) HOW A MEMBER GETS ONTO THE FACE'S LIST. contact.accept only marks a row the face already has (contacts.js:606). The face gets a row by peer.acquire, which checks the key is on a relay roll, and your members are on your relay. So grantFace's sync sends two owner commands: peer.acquire { member, relay }, then contact.accept. The face must carry 'peer' as well as 'contact' (face-install, then your rerun on spirit-3), and the passthrough will tell grantFace which relay a member came through.
2) YOUR OWN APPS. The face's 'serve' for a name granted to your own node still lands on appFaceApp's owner half, which hands it to the app's pipe. That half needs name -> app, which grantFace now owns. PICK: grantFace, the one writer, keeps a small mirror in appFaceApp's folder (the names granted to your own node, with their app), and appFaceApp only reads it. No new verb.
3) MIGRATION. appFaceApp stops answering 'grant' and 'route?'; the face sends 'route?' to grantFace instead. Its grant-exchange tests move to grantFace. The face on spirit-3 needs the new code for this, so the face-install rerun becomes part of G19.3.
Go! = these three as picked, and I build G19.3.
